state.context: Review three demonstrated gaps in canlang, an AI-authored company CRUD DSL prioritizing adoption, economical tokens, reliable generation and one canonical primitive per operation. The user authorizes research through implementation with a stop on concrete invalidity. There is no compiler/parser/runtime, executed app acceptance or agent/tokenizer benchmark. Existing primitives have typed models/contracts/unions, field-type reuse, pure derivations, owner transactions, locks, explicit by versus on, call/send, durable schedule and canonical form/action UI plus generated MCP. No framework, service registry file, copied operation signature or editable opaque JSON is an acceptable patch. Assess concrete contracts and alternatives independently; classification is advice, not authorization.
state.calendar: Existing local_date/local_instant/add_days and schedule suffice for explicit dates, day cadence and durable wakeups. They cannot derive a Gregorian month, weekday/year or finite date sequence from the current closed builtin set. CanMember requires original-anchor month-end clamping/restoration, Leave needs cross-year attribution and exact calendar coverage, Book needs weekly/holiday expansion and Rent needs atomic access segments for day pricing. Proposal adds only pure add_months(date,int)->date, date_year(date)->int, weekday(date)->int and dates(from,until,limit)->date[]. Addition clamps the original day in the target month; each recurrence uses the original immutable anchor and absolute offset, never a prior clamp. Dates are Gregorian, weekday ISO Monday1..Sunday7, and range ascending half-open; equal endpoints empty, reversed/overflow/nonpositive limit/over-limit errors, no truncation. Existing add_days is date+calendar days; durations remain elapsed24h days. local_instant retains explicit earlier/later fold and nonexistent-time rejection. Temporal documents clamp/reject date overflow; RFC5545 instead skips invalid recurrence dates, so RRULE is not automatically the billing rule. Alternatives are authoritative pre-expanded dates using existing operations, interoperable RRULE recurrence with explicit divergent semantics, or deferral. Helpers add scalar signatures and bounds; pre-expanded dates avoid grammar but shift work/authority to producers; RRULE adds substantial parser/policy surface. Targeted sources use manager term boundaries and Leave derived years/coverage. Automatic renewal admission/recovery, host/location hours and all-segment day holds remain app-owned work, not implied by date helpers.
state.retention: Existing delete requires generated CRUD deletion enabled, so technical histories have no path; loosening that alone is insufficient because locks forbid removal through any path and archive preserves sensitive values/files. User CRUD must remain absent/disabled. Candidate retain Model until=expr declares a pure non-null owner-local datetime lifetime in row scope. Runtime expires whole records/subtrees at deadline<=admitted now, including archived rows, independently of CRUD. It explicitly authorizes removal of expired immutable data, never changes/early deletion of locked values. A child without a lifetime inherits parent expiry; an independent child deadline cannot exceed parent and conflicts are rejected on affected writes/config changes. Catch splits raw file ownership from normalized Occurrence; raw receipt-based30d and Issue last-activity90d are independent declarations, with raw_days<=issue_days explicit config validation. Stats expires validated activity at30d and rechecks age in queued processing; Check declares90d developer history setting. Lifecycle expiry is irreversible under the owner fence; configuration changes affect unexpired rows only and cannot resurrect expired retained storage. Queries/downloads deny expired content. Bounded runtime scans make incremental progress without changing for limit into truncation. Removal preserves invariants/references: every stored incoming reference outside the removed set blocks physical disposal; incompatible/cyclic/cross-owner removal reports blocked. Reference release commits before retryable R2 deletion; shared valid references protect objects. Expired-data audit snapshots/outbox content must also be disposed under the declared lifecycle, keeping only safe attribution/outcome and owner-scoped keyed dedup digests for the retry horizon; replay cannot become a new event when business history expires. Physical erasure delays/backlogs/blocks are observable and not called successful purge. Alternative separate model deletion policy plus trusted delete handlers allows explicit schedule/control but needs a bounded batch mechanism and explicit lifetime exception to removal locks; generic external TTL lacks local relational/lock/audit coordination. A retention declaration costs runtime dependency/lifecycle work and constrained expiry semantics; it is not already expressible unchanged. No universal TTL, privilege bypass or generic maintenance tool is proposed.
state.delegation: CanDo has operation/source strings and opaque JSON inputs, no owner input form, missing reference matching, discarded delivery and transport-only freshness. Real owner operations include maintain.inspect with inspection/answers/result/evidence, plus success/onboard/board/volunteer completion, with current guards retained. Proposed action(Target,...) is a finite type over statically imported user operations; action(Target,{record bindings}) constructs without execution, binding all record-typed parameters/versions only and leaving other business inputs for existing form. No text conversion, arbitrary schema or ambient targets; constructor cannot manufacture remote trust. Export owner operation/model declarations and bind imports explicitly; owner signatures/results/descriptions/constraints generate schemas. Trusted WorkSources replies provide sealed action handles tied to configured source, target/interface revision, principal/team and protected record/version; runtime rejects unknown origins, substitution, tampering, expiry/stale projection and access loss. form row.action renders same canonical inputs, hides bound records, and offers no submit when null. Calls stay local atomic, sends remote asynchronous. Runtime correlation/receipt keys include binding/target/record/revision/principal/team/operation_id; queued/pending/failed/conflict/unknown/fulfilled remain distinct. Fulfilled means owner commit, not work completion; invalidate old handle and requery source before changing source item state. Remote authorization uses separate audience-specific credentials, never forwarding incoming tokens or accepting actor/team input. Generated per-target MCP schemas retain canonical business inputs and an explicit closed ordinary-versus-action_handle envelope where exposed; fixed record bindings make remaining inputs stable. UI typed controls reject opaque JSON. WorkBatch carries bounded items and unique statuses for the finite expected sources; success of transport alone is not fresh. Existing refresh remains; no imaginary automatic poll/source adapter is claimed. Alternatives: operation-input type projections and finite union/router through existing perform, with routing/variant maintenance but no copied signatures; static owner forms/typed rows, reusing more existing grammar but repeating per-source layout and needing defined remote dispatch/narrowing. Action references add type/storage/seal/dispatch semantics and couple to interface changes. They avoid per-source input duplication, not all integration implementation.

calendar_choice.instructions: Which calendar mechanism best closes the specified reusable gap?

criteria.pure_helpers: Extend the existing pure date vocabulary with the four bounded helpers, keeping schedule unchanged.
criteria.expanded_dates: Use only existing primitives and supply authoritative pre-expanded dates from outside.
criteria.rrule: Adopt general recurrence-rule syntax with explicitly reconciled month-end and DST semantics.
criteria.unresolved: Keep the calendar mechanism undecided if these alternatives remain invalid or insufficient.

retention_choice.instructions: Which cleanup mechanism best meets these evidence and constraints?

criteria.declared_expiry: Declare model lifetimes with retain and implement owner-scoped bounded lifecycle disposal.
criteria.trusted_delete: Separate model deletion policy from user CRUD and use explicit trusted handlers plus reviewed expiry/removal rules.
criteria.external_ttl: Move disposal to external TTL infrastructure with explicit synchronization of references and evidence.
criteria.unresolved: Leave retention design open if none establishes a coherent lifecycle.

delegation_choice.instructions: Which typed form mechanism best fits the described heterogeneous queue?

criteria.bounded_action: Use finite operation-valued action references through the existing form/registry.
criteria.input_union: Derive owner input types and route a closed union through the existing perform operation.
criteria.static_forms: Bind each supported owner operation to existing static forms with typed source rows.
criteria.unresolved: Do not select a mechanism until the remaining typing/authority issues can be resolved.

calendar_contract.instructions: Does the proposed pure date contract define anchored clamping, bounded ranges and existing zone behavior consistently for these cases?

retention_contract.instructions: Can the declared lifetime rules coexist with immutable values, owner authority, references and retry/file/audit obligations without an identified contradiction?

delegation_contract.instructions: Do the finite action and schema/delegation contracts define typed inputs and current owner authorization coherently, keeping source state distinct from invocation outcome?
